method: Independent manual review of saved final answers, candidate/verifier feedback and supplied passages; local Corpus text/hash/outline validation. No new model scoring, paid calls, backend mutation or browser control.
pass_definition: useful_pass requires the planned task behavior to be delivered; caveats are reported independently. A source-check pass is not the human usefulness judgment, and useful does not imply every sentence is perfectly grounded.

cases.verifier_failure: Overstrict feedback weakened a supported connection; final answer also lacks requested review timing distinction.

checks.reason: Curated evaluation is explained, but monitoring completed live turns is not. No remote-scorer timing passage was read in this turn.

checks.reason: No claim that Signals intercept, prevent, or modify delivered answers.

findings.rejection: Signals score or tag recorded activity in production is slightly over-composed.

Signals surface quality and safety issues to flag problems, find patterns, and highlight the traces that need your attention.

findings.assessment: The passages establish agent-turn scoring and production traces directly. Demanding more support for this ordinary connection was overstrict; this is separate from the absent completed-turn timing evidence.
Rejecting a negative claim about the entire snapshot after reading a few sections was justified. Qualifying that limited research was appropriate.

cases.comparison_to_v1: The v1 case returned only an insufficient-evidence message; v2 supplies supported roles and a Dataset connection. This is an improvement in this selected execution, not a full planned-check pass or causal benchmark.

checks.reason: Same conversation_id and retained actual previous question/answer; prior S1 remains identifiable.

checks.check: Explains post-turn monitoring versus separately implemented synchronous checks.
checks.reason: S6 establishes scoring after completed turns and asynchronous feedback. S7 establishes app code applying a scorer and choosing original response or fallback before returning.

checks.check: Makes no safety or correctness guarantee.
checks.reason: No guarantee of perfect safety/correctness. The answer identifies the cookbook as simple phrase matching.

findings.severity: Precision caveat only; not a failed task check or evidence that the practical advice is wrong.
findings.answer_claim: Signals don't block anything. They score and flag agent turns after the fact.

evidence.excerpt: Log one completed turn, then check the **Signals** tab. Scoring is asynchronous, so the result appears after a delay.
A remote scorer signal scores each completed agent turn with an HTTP endpoint that you host, instead of with an LLM judge.

findings.assessment: In the context of the question, the opening means Signals should not be relied on to block delivery of an unsafe response. The supplied remote-scorer timing and runtime-guardrail example support that useful distinction. The body explicitly narrows its timing evidence to remote scorers and acknowledges unseen features. Leading with that scope would be more precise, but a worst-case universal reading should not turn the otherwise useful answer into a failure.

Correctly labels the runtime scorer example as Calls-based and separate from Agents/Signals; does not claim apply_scorer can be called on an Agent span. It does not claim the cookbook code was executed.
The direct opening and concrete alternative are useful. The trailing caveats are longer than needed and partly contradict the opening certainty.

cases.finding_interpretation: Evaluate the phrase in the user question and full-answer context. The precision caveat does not change useful_pass=true or the three passing planned checks.

limits: Two selected cases in one conversation, one execution each; no population accuracy or causal speed/cost claim.
Support mode does not assess whole-task completeness; independent review still checks the prewritten scenario requirements.
No grading was changed and original answers/verdicts remain intact.
The historical interrupted UI traces and v1 insufficient response are distinct observations; this review does not infer who initiated any historical request.
